newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: General Signal to grab Asian opportunities.
newsitem.headline: General Signal to grab Asian opportunities.

text.p: U.S. company General Signal is putting more resources into Asia as part of a bid to chalk up further record earnings, its chairman and chief executive officer Michael Lockhart said on Thursday.
"We expect another record year...sales and profits," in 1997, Lockhart told reporters at the opening of its Singapore office.
"The first thing is to get the sales growth...Obviously increasing our participation in this (Asia) market is the single best thing we can do," he said.

General Signal has 15 business units making products for the process control, electrical control and industrial technology industries. For the financial year ended December 31 1996, it recorded a net profit of US$133.4 million on record sales of US$2.07 billion.
Lockhart said for the company to hit another record year, it would also have to improve productivity, which means making its products less expensive.
"Part of making them less expensive is to do more manufacturing here and to source more of our raw materials (components) from this region," he said.
General Signal would be investing US$10 million over the next five years in Asia with US$2.0-4.0 million for new plant investments. Asia excludes Australia, he said.
The investments would be funded from internal resources, he said.
To date General Signal has pumped in about US$50 million in Asia and Australia in capital investment, he said.
The company was likely to set up a plant for ultra-low temperature freezers for use in the life-sciences industry, for instance to store tissue samples and to store blood, he said.
Locations being considered were in Malaysia and China, officials said.
Currently, the company has four wholly-owned plants in Asia manufacturing mixers and coal feeders.
Lockhart said General Signal had five joint ventures in the region and was likely to undertake more partnerships. It was increasing its distributors in the region as well.
Asia now contributes 7-8 percent to its worldwide revenue and Lockhart expected revenues from the region to double in 1997.
He saw the proportion of contribution from Asia doubling in about five years' time.
"We believe we haven't taken full advantage of the opportunities here," he said, adding that General Signal was looking for "balance" in its various businesses across the region.
